record.paper_title: An Experimental Mathematics Perspective on the Old, and still Open, Question of When To Stop?
record.original_question: Let β_n denote the Chow-Robbins stopping boundary after n tosses, meaning that one should stop as soon as the number of heads minus the number of tails is at least β_n. The paper highlights the specific unresolved case n = 8: is β_8 equal to 2? Equivalently, after eight tosses with five heads and three tails, is it optimal in the infinite-horizon game to stop immediately and take the certain payoff 5/8 = 0.625, or to continue playing because the true expected payoff from that state eventually exceeds 5/8?

evidence.quote: It tells us nothing, for example, about the still open β8 (presumably 2) and not even about β100 .
For example, the still-open question whether β8 = 2 can be phrased as follows. If currently you have five heads and three tails, should you stop?
If you stop, you can definitely collect 5/8 = 0.625, whereas if you keep going, your expected gain is > 0.6235, but no one currently knows to prove that it would not eventually exceeds 5/8

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem (the Chow–Robbins game). A fair coin is tossed repeatedly. After any number of tosses the player may stop; if the player stops after a total of n tosses with H heads and T = n − H tails, the payoff is H/n. The player may also continue forever (in which case the payoff is the limit, which is 1/2 almost surely). Let V(H,T) denote the supremum, over all stopping rules, of the expected payoff starting from a state with H heads and T tails already accumulated. It is known that the optimal policy has the form: stop in state (H,T) with n = H + T tosses if and only if H − T ≥ β_n, for a sequence of integer thresholds β_n.

Question: Is β_8 = 2? Equivalently, in the state with H = 5 heads and T = 3 tails (so the current empirical mean is 5/8 = 0.625), is it optimal to stop immediately, i.e., does V(5,3) = 5/8? Determine whether stopping is optimal in the position (H,T) = (5,3), or whether instead V(5,3) > 5/8.
artifact.status_search_result: Häggström and Wästlund (arXiv:1201.0626, 2012/2013) gave a rigorous computer analysis of the Chow–Robbins game and determined the optimal action in many previously unresolved early positions, including the position with 5 heads and 3 tails; the position (5,3) belongs to the stopping set, confirming β_8 = 2. Subsequent work (e.g., the Catalan-triangle approach, arXiv:2205.13499, 2022) reaffirmed exact solutions for almost all n.

status_evidence.title: Rigorous computer analysis of the Chow-Robbins game
status_evidence.snippet: Häggström and Wästlund use upper and lower bounds and backward induction to decide optimal stopping in early positions of the Chow–Robbins game.
status_evidence.claim: They resolved the previously unclear position (5,3), showing it lies in the stopping set, i.e. β_8 = 2.

status_evidence.title: Exact Solution to the Chow-Robbins Game for almost all n, using the Catalan Triangle
status_evidence.snippet: Provides exact solutions to the Chow–Robbins game for almost all n via the Catalan triangle.
status_evidence.claim: Later work confirms and extends the exact determination of stopping thresholds β_n.
